title: 75% of Rural Habitations Covered with Sujal Gaon IDs under Jal Jeevan Mission Across States/UTs
subtitle: Sujal Gaon and Sujalam Bharat IDs Strengthen Digital Governance of Rural Water Supply Under JJM
body_text:
The Sujal Gaon ID is a unique identification number assigned under the digital monitoring framework of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 for water supply service area (habitation/s) meeting the prescribed standards and criteria under the Mission. The ID is issued through the national JJM digital platform and the details are communicated to the respective States/UTs through the JJM digital ecosystem. The objective of the Sujal Gaon ID is to facilitate systematic identification, monitoring, reporting, tracking and verification of water supply service area (habitation/s) achieving desired outcomes in rural drinking water service delivery and sustainability. As on 10.08.2026, out of 16,96,213 habitations in the country, Sujal Gaon IDs have been issued to 12,67,808 habitations (75%) across all States/UTs.
Sujalam Bharat has been developed as a federated Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) for lifecycle-based and service-oriented management of Rural Piped Water Supply Schemes (RPWSS). It integrates digital asset registries, geospatial mapping and decision-support systems to provide unified visibility of water supply infrastructure. Integrated with the PM GatiShakti platform, it provides a GIS-validated architecture and assigns unique digital identities to rural water supply schemes through Sujalam Bharat IDs.
Sujal Gaon IDs and Sujalam Bharat IDs under the Jal Jeevan Mission provide unique digital identities to service areas and rural water supply schemes, respectively. Their integration with GIS and structured hydraulic linkages enables end-to-end source-to-tap mapping, asset tracking and lifecycle management. This facilitates better planning, monitoring and accountability of existing schemes, helps identify gaps and duplication, and enables data-driven decision-making and effective Operation and Maintenance (O&M). Thus, these digital IDs strengthen transparency and oversight and help reduce irregularities in the implementation of JJM.
This information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI SHRI V. SOMANNA in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Jal Shakti informed the Lok Sabha that as of 10 August 2026, Sujal Gaon IDs have been issued to 12,67,808 out of 16,96,213 rural habitations (75%) across India under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 digital monitoring framework. These unique IDs, along with Sujalam Bharat IDs assigned to rural piped water supply schemes, form a federated Digital Public Infrastructure integrated with GIS mapping and the PM GatiShakti platform for tracking water supply infrastructure. The system enables source-to-tap mapping, asset tracking, lifecycle management and improved transparency in JJM implementation.
enrichment.context:
The Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), launched in 2019, aims to provide Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTC) to every rural household in India, and has since evolved to JJM 2.0 which emphasizes not just coverage but service sustainability, quality, and digital governance. As the mission matures from a construction-heavy phase to an operation-and-maintenance (O&M) phase, digital tools like Sujal Gaon IDs and Sujalam Bharat IDs become critical for ensuring assets created are tracked, functional, and accountable over their lifecycle, rather than becoming defunct infrastructure.

The integration with PM GatiShakti — India's national master plan for multi-modal infrastructure connectivity using GIS-based planning — reflects a broader governance trend of using Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) to unify data across sectors, reduce duplication of efforts, and enable evidence-based policymaking. This approach mirrors similar digital ID systems in other sectors (e.g., Aadhaar for individuals, GSTIN for businesses) applied to physical infrastructure and geographic service areas, marking a shift toward asset-level digital governance in rural development schemes.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Sujal Gaon ID' mentioned in news is associated with which of the following schemes?
prelims_questions.explanation: Sujal Gaon ID is a unique identification number assigned under the digital monitoring framework of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 to habitations meeting prescribed water supply service standards.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements about 'Sujalam Bharat' under the Jal Jeevan Mission:
1. It is a federated Digital Public Infrastructure for managing Rural Piped Water Supply Schemes.
2. It is integrated with the PM GatiShakti platform.
3. It assigns unique digital identities only to individual households, not to schemes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: Sujalam Bharat is a federated DPI for lifecycle management of Rural Piped Water Supply Schemes, integrated with PM GatiShakti, and assigns Sujalam Bharat IDs to schemes (not individual households), making statement 3 incorrect.

mains_questions.question: Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) is increasingly being used to strengthen governance of rural welfare schemes. Discuss with reference to the Sujal Gaon and Sujalam Bharat IDs under the Jal Jeevan Mission how such digital identity systems can improve accountability and sustainability of infrastructure.

Examine the challenges in ensuring long-term sustainability of rural piped water supply schemes in India. How can integration of GIS-based digital monitoring frameworks like Sujalam Bharat with initiatives such as PM GatiShakti help address these challenges?
